title: LoopRPT: Reinforcement Pre-Training for Looped Language Models
claim: Explicit step-by-step reasoning is costly and can degrade; compressing reasoning into adaptive latent iterations is more accurate and efficient.
layout: 2 panels: left flowchart contrast (explicit vs latent), right grouped bar chart; funnel device
description: The left panel (a) is a side-by-side flowchart contrast. Under the same input, 'What is 12 * 14?', the Standard LM branch on the left splits into direct generation and a four-step explicit chain-of-thought. Direct generation uses a gear-brain icon, fails on hard tokens, and gives the incorrect '156'. The CoT chain is in red and ends in a correct but slow and costly '168'. The Looped LM branch on the right is blue. It shows hidden states h0, h1 and h2 inside a shaded funnel, with easy, medium and hard loop markers, an exit gate with a threshold toggle, and a green correct, efficient output. The right panel (b) is a grouped bar chart of next-token reasoning accuracy across Easy, Medium and Hard. It compares Qwen3 vanilla, Qwen3 CoT and Ouro-1.4B, and annotates the gains of Ouro-1.4B in percent.
caption: Motivation for LoopRPT. (a) Standard LLMs reason through explicit chain-of-thought tokens, whereas LoopLMs compress multi-step reasoning into latent space. (b) LoopLMs achieve higher next-token-reasoning accuracy than standard LLMs across difficulty levels.
abstract: Looped language models (LoopLMs) perform iterative latent computation to refine internal representations, offering an alternative to explicit chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning. However, existing reinforcement learning (RL) paradigms primarily target output tokens, creating a structural mismatch with looped architectures whose reasoning unfolds implicitly. In this work, we propose LoopRPT, a reinforcement pre-training framework tailored for LoopLMs. By reframing next-token prediction as a next-token reasoning task, LoopRPT assigns reinforcement signals directly to latent steps using an EMA teacher reference and noisy latent rollouts. This formulation enables RL to directly shape intermediate representations, compressing effective reasoning into fewer iterations. We instantiate LoopRPT on Ouro across multiple model scales. Results show that LoopRPT improves per-step representation quality and achieves Pareto dominance in accuracy-computation trade-offs. Large gains on hard tokens indicate that LoopRPT enhances early-stage reasoning rather than merely encouraging premature exits. Our findings highlight reinforcement pre-training as a principled paradigm for learning efficient latent reasoning in LoopLMs.
